commits.message:
decodeAnsi's cells hold tabs and leave escapes whole, and a URL holds no census code point (rich-control-codes-xh4n.fng)

Review of #536. The cell model read a tab as zero-width, so a redraw lost it and
the text after it; a tab now moves to the next stop. Line breaks were rewritten
before tokenizing, which cut an OSC payload in two and leaked its tail as text.
What has no width at the first column waited in a slot nothing cleared, so it
outlived an erase and piled up across redraws; it now joins the next cell drawn.

stripUrlControls derives from the census: an explicit bidi control or LS still
reached the bytes in an OSC 8 URL, around `sealed`.

decodeAnsi counts cells and Syntax escapes what it deleted (rich-control-codes-xh4n.fng)

Review of #536. A backspace moved one code point, so a redraw over wide or
combining text landed on the wrong characters; columns are now a terminal's
cells, and a C1 control takes none. decodeAnsi breaks at the census's line breaks.

Syntax deleted a bare CR, C1 and explicit bidi controls, so `// note\reval(x)`
showed one comment line while a compiler ran the call. It escapes them now.

Console.bell reads who is at the terminal, not forceInteractive.

C0 controls keep their meaning, and content writes no directive (rich-control-codes-xh4n.fng)

VT and FF are line breaks, and the codes with no meaning in a span show their
Control Pictures symbol, one code unit for one. BEL's alert is Console.bell, and
BS's overstrike and ESC's styling are decodeAnsi, which reads nroff's grammar.

sealed is total: only keep and an admitted withheld code point reach the wire, so
a raw Segment, a widget label, an end and a TextInput value are contained by one
rule. A link's URL takes no C0 or C1 at stripUrlControls. Syntax escapes what the
wire refuses, so a line number stays the editor's.

Format characters keep their meaning in content, and their abuse is contained (rich-control-codes-xh4n.5do) (#535)

* Format characters keep their meaning in content, and their abuse is contained (rich-control-codes-xh4n.5do)

The census gains two dispositions. `line-break` turns U+2028 and U+2029 into an
LF at the content boundary, code unit for code unit, so every reader of a Text
finds one line ending. `withheld` covers the soft hyphen, tag characters and
variation selectors: content keeps them, and `replaceWithheld` decides from their
neighbours what reaches the wire. It runs in `sealed`, on text nothing cuts again,
so a rule that reads context cannot move an offset. `cellLen` measures what it
leaves, and a deletion keeps every cluster boundary the text had, so a cut stays
exact.

The wrapper breaks where a word's own text says it may: after ZWSP, at a soft
hyphen, which draws as `-` only at a break it took, and between the words of Thai,
Lao, Khmer and Burmese. U+FEFF stops counting as a space, which was JavaScript's
`\s` departing from Rich by accident. JSON escapes whatever content or the wire
would drop, so it parses back to its data.

Departures from Rich: a soft hyphen measures 0 rather than 1, and a U+2028 in a
JSON string prints as an escape. docs/control-codes.md records each family and
what tmux, Terminal.app, iTerm2 and xterm.js were measured doing.

* A break, a measure and a document each read what is drawn (rich-control-codes-xh4n.5do)

High review of #535. A run's start is no break, a mark with no text before it
neither; a zero-width code point after a wrap's whitespace is not content; a
text's edge is the last thing drawn; a value's own separator lays out as an LF;
JSON has one escape pass over the census; the two per-render fast paths return.

* The hanging whitespace test renders the text itself, since print sets its own overflow and justify (rich-control-codes-xh4n.5do)

* A row's tail and a word's ends are read from what is drawn, and Pretty shows what the wire withholds (rich-control-codes-xh4n.5do)

Medium review of #535. drawnTail answers the tail once for hanging whitespace and
a filled line, in linear time, and leaves a mark on a space as content. A break
needs a glyph on both sides. Pretty escapes what a string would lose on the wire,
and a value's own text is wired before it is laid out.

* Syntax escapes what the wire withholds, and a soft hyphen costs nothing it cannot draw (rich-control-codes-xh4n.5do)

Second high review of #535. Code on show escapes withheld code points through the
one unicodeEscape Pretty uses. A run of marks is one break, a zero-cell piece takes
no hyphen, and a piece's minimum is its own cells. edges counts a tab. hyphenated
walks a segment once, and replaceWithheld returns text it did not touch.
